comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory NRV Write-Downs Mechanics and Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company recorded inventory write-downs to NRV due to declining ASPs for DRAM and NAND; these pre-recorded charges resulted in lower subsequent cost of goods sold when the inventory was sold, with the net impact reflecting current period write-downs offset by lower costs from prior period written-down inventory.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose specific cost of sales charges related to inventory valuation. Intel reports $695 million in higher period charges for excess capacity and inventory reserves in 2023, which reduced total cost of sales. Micron details its policy of writing down inventory to net realizable value (NRV) due to declining average selling prices (ASPs) in 2023. While Intel cites inventory reserves as an offset to other cost reductions, Micron explains that these write-downs mechanically lowered subsequent cost of goods sold when the inventory was sold. Both companies highlight inventory reserve/write-down dynamics as a key component of their cost of sales variance analysis.

sentences.text: These cost of sales decreases were partially offset by $695 million of higher period charges in 2023, primarily related to excess capacity charges and higher intersegment inventory reserves taken in 2023.

Inventory NRV write-downs: Our consolidated gross margin was impacted by charges in 2023 to write down inventories to their estimated NRV as a result of declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND.
As charges to write down inventories are recorded in advance of when inventories are sold, costs of goods sold in subsequent periods were lower than they otherwise would be.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company charges cost of sales for inventory provisions to write down inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value, or for obsolete or excess inventory and excess product purchase commitments, requiring management judgment based on inventory levels, future commitments, and market conditions.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA explicitly state that inventory provisions or reserves are charged directly to cost of sales. Intel notes $695 million in higher period charges for 'excess capacity and inventory reserves' in 2023 as part of its cost of sales decrease analysis. Similarly, NVIDIA describes its accounting policy where it charges cost of sales for inventory provisions to write down inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value, or for obsolete/excess inventory. Both disclosures link inventory valuation adjustments directly to the cost of sales line item.

comparisons.peer_summary: QTL EBT as a percentage of revenues increased in fiscal 2024 primarily due to lower cost of sales driven by a decrease in amortization expense related to acquired patents and higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: While Intel's cost of sales variance was driven by volume and reserves, Qualcomm attributes a driver of its EBT margin expansion to 'lower cost of sales driven by a decrease in amortization expense related to acquired patents.' This represents a specific cost of sales component (amortization) that Intel did not cite as a primary driver in its 2023 cost of sales summary. Intel's cost of sales decrease was primarily driven by lower intersegment cost of goods sold from reduced sales volume and factory start-up costs, whereas Qualcomm highlights structural cost improvements in its licensing segment's allocated costs.
